summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — RWE.DE +3%, PCT.L +3%, ENT.L +2%, BGEO.L +2%, SAP.DE +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (DTE.DE -7%, BAB.L -5%, TEP.PA -5%, SGO.PA -3%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: DTE.DE (-7.01%) — €550M share buyback second tranche expired on 30 Jun, removing the stock's key price-floor buyer; compounded by persistent T-Mobile US merger uncertainty after SpaceX acquisition rumours (25 Jun) suppressed fresh demand. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — DTE.DE is a DAX-40 mega-cap telecom (~€135B mkt cap). The decline was structural: a pre-announced buyback expiry plus a weeks-long merger overhang, neither of which generates the sharp intraday signal momentum or news-reactive filters look for.

top_movers.catalyst: Re-rating from June 22 Amprion majority-stake deal (€3.6B, 55% ownership) continued into Q2 close, amplified by Barclays/UBS/JPM Buy reaffirmations and end-of-quarter utilities sector rotation.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. RWE is a €43B DAX-40 regulated utility — too large and low-beta for momentum screens; the Amprion catalyst was announced 8 days prior, leaving no clean same-day signal for a news-reactive strategy to act on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-deal re-rating window: when a large-cap EU utility announces transformative M&A (>€1B deal size), enrol it in the momentum universe for 15 trading days with a relaxed volume floor (≥0.8× avg vs. standard ≥1.5×) to capture the multi-day re-rating tail.

top_movers.catalyst: Global tech rally on 29 Jun (NASDAQ +2.07%, Alphabet +5%, semis +3%+) lifted Polar Capital Technology Trust's underlying portfolio NAV; June 30 daily NAV RNS confirmed the gain and share price followed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. PCT.L is a UK-listed closed-end investment trust (FTSE 250, ~£7.8B AUM) that tracks global technology equities — it acts as a sector fund derivative rather than a single-name operating company, and is categorically excluded from single-stock selection strategies.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change — PCT.L mirrors the global tech NAV and adding it would duplicate exposure already captured by individual tech equity positions. Systematic inclusion would require a separate NAV-discount-compression strategy outside current risk parameters.

top_movers.catalyst: Entain announced 20% divestment of Entain CEE to JV partner EMMA Capital for €425m (£366m) on 2026-06-25, beginning phased full exit; net proceeds earmarked for debt reduction — stock drifted +2.35% further through week-end.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ENT.L is a FTSE 100 regulated-gaming name likely excluded by sector filter. The actionable catalyst (RNS filing) landed 2026-06-25 pre-close; today's move is lagged M&A drift — pre-announcement positioning was the only way to capture it cleanly.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an RNS catalyst watchlist: when a FTSE 100/250 name files a divestment or debt-reduction deal ≥£200m, open a 3-session momentum entry window even for sector-gated names, closing if price reverts below the announcement-day close.

top_movers.catalyst: Post-Investor Day institutional follow-through: Lion Finance Group (formerly Bank of Georgia) hosted a ~100-investor Analyst Day in Tbilisi on 26 Jun (JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, M&G attending), generating buy-side order flow into week-end.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BGEO.L is a FTSE 100-listed EM financial (Georgian + Armenian banking), likely screened out by UK/EU domestic-bank sector filters or by EM-revenue exclusion rules. top_movers.suggestion: When a FTSE 100 name files an LSE RNS tagged 'Investor Day' or 'Capital Markets Day', auto-promote it to the UK watchlist for the following 2 sessions with a ≥1.2× prior-30d average volume confirmation gate to capture the institutional follow-through window.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news; +2.18% reflects Q2 quarter-end window dressing and DAX 15%-cap rebalancing flows, with SAP bouncing from a -3% June 22 sell-off as institutional funds dressed portfolios into H1 close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SAP is a €166B DAX 40 enterprise-software mega-cap, likely excluded by cap-tier or sector screen. Window dressing also pre-positions pre-open, making it inaccessible to reactive intraday signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a DAX 40 end-of-quarter sleeve: on the final 2 sessions of each quarter, buy DAX names within 5% of 52-week high, sized ≤0.5% NAV each, exit next open — capturing window-dressing flows without permanent universe expansion.

top_movers.catalyst: UK-wide defence sector rally after PM Starmer announced a £15bn military spending plan; Melrose advanced with peers Rolls-Royce (+2.6%), BAE Systems (+1.8%), and Babcock (+3.2%) on the same session.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. MRO.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap aerospace-components supplier (~£5.8B market cap); its ~2% gain was pure macro sector rotation on a government-spending headline rather than a company-specific signal that single-stock momentum or news-reactive screens would have captured.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK-defence sector-basket trigger: when the FTSE 350 Aerospace & Defence sub-index moves ≥1.5% intraday, enter constituents with sub-index beta >0.9 (including MRO.L) at open, sizing by ATR; exit same-day close to avoid overnight event risk.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DTE.DE is a DAX-40 mega-cap telecom (~€135B mkt cap). The decline was structural: a pre-announced buyback expiry plus a weeks-long merger overhang, neither of which generates the sharp intraday signal momentum or news-reactive filters look for.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a corporate-action calendar that flags names where a published buyback programme expires within 5 trading days; route flagged names to a short-bias screen so the bot can express support-removal risk if the name enters a compatible universe.

top_movers.catalyst: UK MoD confirmed cancellation of the Type 83 destroyer programme on 29 Jun; Babcock was a leading build-contract bidder, removing a multi-billion-pound pipeline opportunity and compounding the £140M Type 31 frigate charge disclosed 22 Jun.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BAB.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap defence contractor (~£5B mkt cap). The move was driven by a discrete government policy cancellation announced pre-open; no technical or momentum signal could have provided advance positioning.
top_movers.suggestion: Expand the news-reactive strategy's universe to include FTSE 100 defence names (BAB.L, BA.L) with a 60-min post-RNS entry window triggered on MoD contract cancellation/award keywords; gate with a £1B+ mkt cap filter to limit universe bloat.

top_movers.catalyst: Concentrix (CNXC) slashed FY2026 revenue guidance to $9.93–10.03B and EPS to $10.83–11.18 on June 30, citing client spending cuts and AI displacement; TEP.PA fell in sector sympathy as RBC called CXO outsourcing 'uninvestable'.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — TEP.PA is a large-cap French BPO services name on Euronext Paris not covered by any current strategy. The move was peer-contagion from a US competitor's earnings miss, not predictable from TEP.PA's own pre-market price or volume signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-contagion gate: when a US CXO/BPO peer (CNXC, TDCX) gaps down >10% on earnings, auto-flag correlated Euronext names sharing the same GICS sub-industry (2520/5020) for short review within 30 min of EU cash open.
